concepts.def: Stored-program computer with CPU, memory, I/O; control and data share bus (Von Neumann 1945 EDVAC report).
Arithmetic Logic Unit, Control Unit, registers (MAR, MDR, PC, IR, accumulator); fetch-decode-execute cycle.
Small fast SRAM between CPU and RAM; L1, L2, L3 levels; exploits temporal/spatial locality.
Primary (RAM, cache) volatile, fast; secondary (HDD, SSD) non-volatile, slower, larger.
Manages CPU scheduling, memory, file systems, I/O, security; UNIX 1969 (Thompson & Ritchie).
Base-2 numerals; integers as two's complement; characters via ASCII (1963) or Unicode UTF-8.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Computer Architecture — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Computer Architecture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Computer Architecture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
